key.name: font
key.description: Font family used to render the key glyphs. The default keeps the stylesheet font, which carries a built-in fallback chain (the script-specific IBM Plex Sans siblings, then a generic sans-serif) so glyphs outside the family still render. A custom family is used on its own; the system substitutes a fallback font for any glyph it lacks.

key.name: fkeys
key.description: Maps a function-row slot (f1-f12) to a standard function id. A slot with no entry taps its default function key.

key.name: active-color
key.description: Hex colour drawn on a one-shot or locked modifier. The locked state uses a brighter shade derived from it.

key.name: case
key.description: Case applied to the static key faces (Esc, Tab, Ctrl). The F in F1-F12 always stays uppercase; typed glyphs follow the active layout.

key.name: layout
key.description: Which key block to draw: a 60% compact block, the default 75% block with the function row, navigation column and arrow cluster, or a 100% full block that adds the numpad.

key.name: height
key.description: Keyboard height as a percent of the display height. Being relative to the screen, it holds across resolutions and both orientations.

key.name: spacing
key.description: Spacing between keys as a percent of the default gutter. 100 keeps the default spacing; lower values tighten the gap on both axes, leaving the key and board sizes unchanged.

key.name: glyph-size
key.description: Font size of the key glyphs as a percent of the default. 100 keeps the default size; the scale applies to every label tier at once and leaves the key and board sizes unchanged.

key.name: corner
key.description: Roundness of the key corners. Sharp is nearly square, soft keeps the default rounding, round is fully rounded.

key.name: rounded
key.description: Whether the keyboard's top corners are rounded. When on, a window sliding up behind the transparent corners can flash an artifact; turn it off to square the corners and remove it.

key.name: modifier-mode
key.description: How a soft modifier (Shift, Ctrl, Super, Alt) responds to a tap. Hold: a quick tap is one real keystroke and a long press locks. Latch: a tap arms the next keystroke only and a double tap locks. Toggle: every tap flips a lock.

key.name: accents
key.description: Whether a long press on a Latin letter opens a popup of accented variants. When off, every key repeats on hold instead.

key.name: click-enabled
key.description: Whether tapping a key plays a short click. The click is synthesised and routed through the shell's event-sound channel, so a system mute of event sounds silences it too.

key.name: click-sound
key.description: Which synthesised click to play: thock (deep and warm), click (soft and muted), tap (crisp and tactile) or pop (light and high).

key.name: click-volume
key.description: Loudness of the key click as a percent of full scale. Zero is silent, the same as turning the click off.
